The theory also incorporates superposition, where particles can exist in multiple states simultaneously until measured, and uncertainty principles, which limit the precision with which certain pairs of physical properties can be known. These principles were developed through groundbreaking experiments and theories by pioneering scientists such as Max Planck, Albert Einstein, Niels Bohr, and Erwin Schrödinger, revolutionizing our understanding of the microscopic realm.  

Quantum mechanics has profound implications for our view of reality and underpins many modern technologies.
